mainTopic: Claims and denials of קידושין: whose words bind whom, and whether קידושין with one witness counts
overview: The amud opens by finishing the case of a father who said he betrothed 'my elder daughter' to a man but does not know which daughter he meant. The גמרא explains why רבי מאיר does not permit a middle daughter of the second group: in that case there are only two daughters there. It then answers a challenge from the case of פסח, showing that the argument there is only about the meaning of the words 'עד פני הפסח'. A new משנה follows. When a man and a woman disagree about whether there was קידושין, each one is bound only by his or her own claim. The גמרא explains why each case of the משנה is needed and learns that a mother is not believed about her daughter's קידושין. It then works out what the בית דין does when she claims קידושין and he denies it: it asks him to give a גט, and if he gives one on his own, it forces him to pay the כתובה. Finally, שמואל rules that קידושין in front of one witness does not count, even if both sides admit it. רבא challenges this ruling from two משניות, and the גמרא answers each challenge by explaining that משנה's case differently. The second answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The middle daughter of the second group should be permitted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה: a middle daughter of the second group should also be permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: The middle daughter of the second group should be permitted!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a problem. According to רבי מאיר in the משנה, only the youngest of the second group is permitted, but a middle daughter of that group should also be permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's doubt is about whom he meant by 'my elder daughter': the eldest of the first group, the eldest of the second group, or the youngest of the first group, who is still older than all of the second group. A middle daughter of the second group is not one of these options. Yet רבי מאיר's wording, 'all are forbidden except the youngest of the second group,' forbids her. The גמרא wants to know why.

keyTerms.meaning: the middle one (the middle daughter)
the second group (daughters of the second wife)
she should be permitted

phrases.english: The middle daughter of the second group should be permitted!
phrases.notes: The 'second group' is the daughters of his second wife, who are all younger than the first wife's daughters.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the analysis of the משנה from the previous page.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מאיר's ruling in the משנה that everyone is forbidden except the youngest of the second group.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A middle daughter of the second group is not one of the daughters he could have meant by 'the elder' (the eldest of either group, or the youngest of the first group), so she should be permitted. The משנה's wording seems to forbid her.

steps.title: The second group has only two daughters
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה's case has only an older and a younger daughter in the second group.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here we are dealing with a case where there are only an older one and a younger one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the case in the משנה has no middle daughter in the second group at all. There are only two daughters there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumed there was a middle daughter. The answer changes the setup of the case: with only two daughters, 'except the youngest' simply means everyone else is forbidden. So no middle daughter is being forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Here, what case are we dealing with? (a formula that narrows the case)
the older one
the younger one

phrases.english: Here, what are we dealing with?
Where there are only an older one and a younger one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 1.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The second group includes a middle daughter, who should be permitted.
steps.terutzMaskana: The second group has only two daughters, so no middle daughter is being forbidden.

steps.title: Support: otherwise the משנה would have mentioned her
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues that its answer makes sense, because a middle daughter would have been mentioned if she existed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so too it is reasonable: if there were a middle daughter, the משנה should have taught about her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds support for its answer. If the second group had a middle daughter, the משנה would have said something about her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof comes from what the משנה leaves out. A middle daughter of the second group would be a real case of doubt that needs to be spelled out. Since the משנה is silent about her, she probably does not exist in this case.

keyTerms.meaning: and so too it is reasonable (a formula introducing support)
if it were so
let it teach her (the משנה should mention her)

phrases.english: And so too it is reasonable,
for if it were so that there is one, let it teach her.
phrases.notes: 'One' means a middle daughter in the second group, and 'it' is the משנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings logical support for the answer in step 2.
steps.raayaObject: That the second group has only two daughters.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה does not mention a middle daughter of the second group.

steps.title: But the middle daughter of the first group is not mentioned either
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: the משנה also leaves out the first group's middle daughter, and she certainly exists in the doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to your reasoning, the middle daughter of the first group is certainly in doubt and forbidden to him. Does the משנה teach about her?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the support from step 3. The משנה also does not mention the middle daughter of the first group, even though she is clearly forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If silence proved that a daughter does not exist, it would also prove that the first group has no middle daughter. But the משנה clearly forbids such a daughter. So silence may prove nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: and according to your reasoning
a doubt
she is forbidden
does it teach her? (a challenging question)

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning, the middle daughter of the first group,
who is certainly part of the doubt and forbidden to him,
does the משנה teach about her?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the support brought in step 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the supporting proof from step 3, not the answer of step 2 itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה also leaves out a daughter who clearly exists and is forbidden, so its silence proves nothing.

steps.title: The first group's middle daughter is already covered
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the comparison: forbidding the first group's youngest already includes the middle one, who is older than her.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can you compare? There, the משנה taught that the youngest of that group is forbidden, and the same rule applies to the one older than her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends its proof. The first group's middle daughter did not need to be mentioned, because the משנה already forbade someone younger than her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה forbids even the youngest of the first group. The middle daughter is older and closer to being 'the elder,' so she is obviously forbidden too. Leaving her out tells us nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: How can you compare? (rejects a comparison)
and the same rule applies
who is older than her

phrases.english: How can you compare?!
There, the משנה taught the youngest of her group as forbidden,
phrases.notes: 'There' is the first group. The משנה forbade its youngest daughter.

phrases.english: and the same applies to this one who is older than her,
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the middle daughter of the first group.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the challenge of step 4 and restores the proof of step 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The comparison between the two middle daughters made in step 4.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The first group's middle daughter is obviously included ('והוא הדין'), because the משנה forbids even the younger daughter of her group. The second group's middle daughter is not covered by any other ruling.

steps.title: Here, a middle daughter would have needed mention
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that a middle daughter of the second group would have needed to be mentioned, so the proof stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here, if there were a middle daughter, the משנה should have taught about her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its argument. In the second group, nothing else in the משנה covers a middle daughter, so the משנה would have had to name her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No ruling about any other daughter would teach us that a middle daughter of the second group is forbidden. One might even think she is permitted, since she is not the eldest. So the משנה's silence shows she does not exist, and the answer of step 2 is confirmed.

keyTerms.meaning: let it teach her

steps.whatToRemember: The second group in the משנה has only two daughters. The משנה would have had to mention a middle daughter there. The first group's middle daughter did not need mention, because forbidding the younger one already includes her.

phrases.english: Here, if it were so that there is one, let the משנה teach her.
phrases.notes: 'Here' is the second group, where no other ruling covers a middle daughter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the contrast begun in step 5 and confirms the proof of step 3.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה's case has only two daughters in the second group, so no middle daughter is being forbidden there.

steps.title: A challenge from the case of Passover
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע asks רבא: the case of פסח is like 'one group', yet the תנאים disagree there.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא son of רב יהושע said to רבא: But look at the case of פסח. It is like 'one group', and still they disagree!
steps.whatsHappening: A new challenge is raised against the claim that in a 'one group' case everyone agrees. רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע points to the case of פסח, where there is still an argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The days of פסח are one unit, so they are like a single group. Yet in a case of someone saying 'until פני הפסח', the same תנאים argue. That seems to show they can disagree even in a 'one group' case.

keyTerms.meaning: One group: a single set with no second set to cause confusion
Is comparable to, is like
They disagree

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ לְרָבָא:
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua said to Rava:

phrases.aramaic: הָא פֶּסַח, דְּכִי כַת אַחַת דָּמֵי,
phrases.english: But there is Passover, which is like one group,
phrases.notes: This is the case of someone who uses the phrase 'until פני הפסח'. רבא quotes it in the next step.

phrases.english: and yet they disagree!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא פֶּסַח, דְּכִי כַת אַחַת דָּמֵי, וּפְלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the claim from the previous page that everyone agrees in a 'one group' case, and challenges it from the case of פסח.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that in a 'one group' case there is no argument
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: פסח is a single unit like one group, yet the תנאים disagree about it. So 'one group' does not rule out an argument.

steps.title: The Passover argument is about how people talk
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the argument about פסח is only about the everyday meaning of the words 'עד פני הפסח'.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: There, they argue about ordinary language. One master holds that 'until פני הפסח' means until before פסח. The other master holds that it means until פסח has passed.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains that the פסח case is a different kind of argument. It is not about the principle being discussed here at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word פני can mean 'before' or 'turning away'. So the argument is about what people mean by that phrase, not about how a person treats a doubtful situation. The rule that everyone agrees in a 'one group' case still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyday language, how people normally talk
'Until פני הפסח': the phrase whose meaning is argued about
Before
Clears away, passes

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a key גמרא move. Two arguments can look alike, but one may be about the meaning of words while the other is about a legal principle.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָתָם בְּלִישָּׁנָא דְעָלְמָא קָמִיפַּלְגִי.
phrases.english: He said to him: There, they disagree about ordinary language.

phrases.aramaic: מָר סָבַר: ״עַד פְּנֵי הַפֶּסַח״ – עַד קַמֵּי פִיסְחָא,
phrases.english: One master holds: 'until פני Passover' means until before Passover,
and the other master holds: until Passover has passed.
phrases.notes: Here פני is read like 'turning away', so the time lasts until פסח is over.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the two cases: the פסח argument is about word meaning, not the principle
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסח argument shows that the תנאים disagree even in a 'one group' case.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסח argument is only about the meaning of the word פני, so the 'one group' rule stays in place.

steps.title: New משנה: he says there was betrothal and she says there wasn't
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that when one side claims קידושין and the other denies it, the one who claims it is bound by the claim. The other side stays free.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One who says to a woman, 'I betrothed you,' and she says, 'You did not betroth me': he is forbidden to her relatives, and she is permitted to his relatives. If she says, 'You betrothed me,' and he says, 'I did not betroth you': he is permitted to her relatives, and she is forbidden to his relatives.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It deals with a man and a woman who disagree about whether קידושין took place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each person is treated as married according to their own words, so they cannot marry the other person's relatives. But one person's claim does not create a marriage for the other, who denies it.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
I betrothed you
Her (female) relatives, such as her sister or mother
Forbidden / permitted

steps.whatToRemember: A person's own claim binds that person. It cannot bind someone who denies it.

phrases.english: MISHNA: One who says to a woman: 'I betrothed you,'
and she says: 'You did not betroth me' —
he is forbidden to her relatives,
and she is permitted to his relatives.
If she says: 'You betrothed me,'
and he says: 'I did not betroth you' —
he is permitted to her relatives,
and she is forbidden to his relatives.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the earlier discussion has ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whoever claims there was קידושין is forbidden to the other person's relatives. The person who denies it remains permitted.

steps.title: He says he betrothed the mother, she says he betrothed her daughter
steps.stepSummary: The man says he betrothed the woman. She says he betrothed only her daughter. He is bound by his claim about the mother, and both women are permitted to his relatives.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he says, 'I betrothed you,' and she says, 'You betrothed only my daughter': he is forbidden to the relatives of the older woman, and the older woman is permitted to his relatives. He is permitted to the relatives of the younger woman, and the younger woman is permitted to his relatives.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with a harder case. The man and the mother each name a different woman as the one he betrothed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man's claim binds only him, so he is forbidden to the mother's relatives. The mother denies her own קידושין, so she is free. Her claim about her daughter does not bind the daughter or the man, so the daughter is free too.

keyTerms.meaning: The older one: here, the mother
The younger one: here, the daughter
My daughter

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'older' and 'younger' do not mean older and younger sisters, as in the earlier case. They mean the mother (older) and her daughter (younger).

phrases.english: If he says 'I betrothed you,' and she says:
'You betrothed only my daughter' —
he is forbidden to the relatives of the older woman,
phrases.notes: The 'older woman' is the mother, the one he claims he betrothed.

phrases.english: and the older woman is permitted to his relatives.
He is permitted to the relatives of the younger woman,
and the younger woman is permitted to his relatives.

steps.triggerLanguage: קִידַּשְׁתִּיךְ וְהִיא אוֹמֶרֶת לֹא קִידַּשְׁתָּ אֶלָּא בִּתִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same rule from step 9 in a case where the two sides name two different women.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each person is bound only by their own claim. The man is forbidden to the mother's relatives, while the mother and the daughter are both permitted to his relatives.

steps.title: He claims the daughter, she claims herself
steps.stepSummary: The משנה's last case: he says he betrothed the daughter, the mother says he betrothed only her. Each one is bound only by his or her own words.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he says 'I betrothed your daughter,' and the mother says 'You betrothed only me,' he is forbidden to the relatives of the younger woman, and the younger woman is permitted to his relatives. He is permitted to the relatives of the older woman, and the older woman is forbidden to his relatives.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the opposite of the case in step 10. Now the man claims the daughter and the mother claims herself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His own claim binds him to the daughter, so he may not marry her relatives. Her claim binds the mother, so she may not marry his relatives. Nobody is bound by what the other person says, so the daughter stays free from his relatives and he stays free from the mother's relatives.

keyTerms.meaning: The younger one, meaning the daughter
The older one, meaning the mother
Female relatives that a man may not marry because of his wife

steps.whatToRemember: Each person is bound only by his or her own claim. A claim never binds the other side.
steps.confusionAlert: קטנה and גדולה here do not mean a minor and an adult girl. They simply mean the younger woman (the daughter) and the older woman (the mother).

phrases.english: "I betrothed your daughter"
and she says
"You betrothed no one but me"
he is forbidden to the relatives of the younger one
phrases.notes: The younger one is the daughter he claims to have betrothed.

phrases.english: and the younger one is permitted to his relatives.
He is permitted to the relatives of the older one
and the older one is forbidden to his relatives.

steps.triggerLanguage: קִדַּשְׁתִּי אֶת בִּתִּךְ וְהִיא אוֹמֶרֶת לֹא קִדַּשְׁתָּ אֶלָּא אוֹתִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The reverse of step 10's case
steps.mimraCoreRuling: He is bound to the daughter by his claim, and the mother is bound by hers. Neither is bound by the other's words.

steps.title: Why the man's case alone would not be enough
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to explain why the משנה teaches both a 'he claims' case and a 'she claims' case. A man's claim might be careless.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: 'One who says to a woman: I betrothed you,' etc. And both cases are needed. If the משנה had taught us only about him, we might say that is because a man does not care, and he just happens to say it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up a צריכותא, an explanation of why the משנה needs two cases that look alike. This step gives the first half: the reason the man's case alone would not teach us enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A man is allowed to marry more than one wife, so saying 'I betrothed you' costs him little, and he might say it carelessly. So his claim is not strong enough to bind the woman. That reason might not apply to a woman's claim, which the next step takes up.

keyTerms.meaning: And it is necessary: the opening of an explanation of why two similar cases are both needed
He does not care
He just happens to say it, without much thought

phrases.english: Gemara: "One who says to a woman: I betrothed you," etc.
And it is necessary
for if it had taught us only about him,
that would be because a man does not care
and he just happens to say it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא now explains the משנה's cases (steps 9-11)
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The man's case alone could be explained by the fact that a man does not take such a claim seriously.

steps.title: Her confident claim still does not bind him
steps.stepSummary: Finishes the צריכותא. We might have trusted the woman's claim enough to bind him too. The משנה teaches that it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: But about her, I would say: if she were not sure of her words, she would not have said them, so he should be forbidden to her relatives. So the משנה teaches us that he is not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes explaining why the woman's case was needed. It ends with קא משמע לן: the משנה teaches us otherwise.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman who says 'he betrothed me' forbids herself to every other man, so she would not say it unless she were sure. We might have thought that makes her claim strong enough to bind him as well. The משנה teaches that even so, her claim binds only her.

keyTerms.meaning: She is sure, she knows it clearly
In her statement, her words
So it teaches us: the answer is the opposite of what we would have thought

steps.whatToRemember: Even a claim that sounds very believable binds only the person who makes it.

phrases.english: But about her, I would say:
if she were not sure of her words,
she would not have said them,
so he should be forbidden to her relatives,
so it teaches us that this is not so.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל אִיהִי, אֵימָא: אִי לָאו דְּקִים לַהּ בְּדִיבּוּרַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the צריכותא begun in step 12
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A woman's confident claim binds only her. It does not forbid the man to her relatives.

steps.title: Why is the mother-and-daughter case needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה needed the case where she says he betrothed only her daughter. The rule was already clear.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'I betrothed you,' and she says, etc. Why do I need this too?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the case where he claims the mother and she says it was her daughter. It asks why the משנה bothered to teach it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule that each person is bound only by his or her own claim was already taught. So this case seems to add nothing new, and the next step will explain what it adds.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need this too? A question about a case that seems extra

phrases.english: "I betrothed you," and she says, etc.
phrases.notes: This is the case from step 10, where she answers, 'You betrothed only my daughter.'

phrases.english: Why do I need this too?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining why the 'he claims' and 'she claims' cases are both needed, the גמרא questions the mother-and-daughter case
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What new idea the case of 'you betrothed only my daughter' teaches

steps.title: A mother is not believed about her daughter
steps.stepSummary: The case was needed so we would not think the רבנן believe a mother about her daughter's קידושין, the way the Torah believes a father.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was needed. You might have thought: by Torah law, the Torah believes a father about his daughter. So by rabbinic law, the רבנן believed the mother, and her daughter would be forbidden by her word. So the משנה teaches us that this is not so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question in step 14. The case teaches that a mother cannot bind her daughter by her claim.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah trusts a father's word about his daughter's קידושין. We might have thought the רבנן gave the mother similar trust, so her words would forbid the daughter. The משנה teaches that she has no such power: her claim binds only herself.

keyTerms.meaning: It was needed
You might have thought: introduces a mistaken first idea
The Torah believes a father
By rabbinic law

steps.whatToRemember: A father is believed about his daughter's קידושין, but a mother is not, not even by rabbinic law.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the father's special trust does not pass to the mother. The basic rule stays in place: a claim binds only the person making it.

phrases.english: It was needed,
since you might have thought:
by Torah law, the Merciful One believes a father,
phrases.notes: The Torah accepts a father's word about his young daughter's קידושין.

phrases.english: so by rabbinic law they believed her,
and her daughter would be forbidden by her word,
so it teaches us that this is not so.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The case teaches that a mother is not believed, even by rabbinic law, to bind her daughter with her claim, unlike a father under Torah law.

steps.title: Why do we need the last case too?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what new lesson comes from the case of 'I betrothed your daughter' when the mother says 'you betrothed only me.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'I betrothed your daughter,' and so on. Why do I need this case too?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps checking each case of the משנה. Now it asks why the משנה needed its very last case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier steps, each case was shown to teach something new. This case is the mirror image of the one before it: he names the daughter, she names herself. The rule that each person is bound only by his or her own words is already clear, so the case looks extra.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need this too? The גמרא's way of asking what a case adds
And so on. The rest of the quote from the משנה is assumed

phrases.english: "I betrothed your daughter," etc.
phrases.notes: The rest of the משנה's line is: and the mother says, 'You betrothed only me.'

phrases.english: Why do I need this one too?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same pattern of questions. Steps 14-15 explained why the earlier case was needed, and now the גמרא asks about the final case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What new teaching comes from the case where he names the daughter and she names herself?

steps.title: It is listed only to complete the set
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the last case teaches nothing new. Since the משנה taught the other version, it taught this one too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the משנה taught that case, it also taught this one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא admits that this case has no new lesson. The משנה listed it to round out all the combinations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not every case in a משנה has to teach a new חידוש. Sometimes the משנה lists all the versions of a situation so the picture is complete. Here, once the משנה taught 'he says the mother, she says the daughter,' it also taught the reverse.

keyTerms.term: אַיְּידֵי דִּתְנָא הָא, תְּנָא נָמֵי הָא
keyTerms.meaning: Since it taught this, it also taught that. A case listed only for completeness

steps.confusionAlert: Do not hunt for a hidden חידוש in this case. The גמרא openly says it is there only because of the case next to it.

phrases.english: Since it taught this one,
phrases.notes: He means the earlier case: he says 'I betrothed you,' and she says 'only my daughter.'

phrases.english: it also taught this one.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַיְּידֵי דִּתְנָא הָא, תְּנָא נָמֵי הָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The case teaches nothing new. It is included only to complete the pair of cases.

steps.title: רב says we force, שמואל says we ask
steps.stepSummary: A new section begins. רב says the בית דין forces the man to give a גט, and שמואל says it only asks him to.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: רב says, we force him. שמואל says, we ask him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new מחלוקת about what the בית דין actually does in these cases. The next steps will work out which case it is about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both אמוראים agree that the man should give a גט. They disagree on how strongly the בית דין may push him. רב says it can force him, and שמואל says it can only ask him politely.

keyTerms.meaning: We force. The בית דין makes him do it
We request. The בית דין only asks him

phrases.english: It was stated:
Rav says: We force,
phrases.notes: He means: we force the man to give a גט.

phrases.english: and Shmuel says: We request.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר, רַב אָמַר: כּוֹפִין, וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: מְבַקְּשִׁין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: how the בית דין handles these cases in practice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: the בית דין forces the man to give a גט. שמואל: it only asks him to.

steps.title: Which case are they arguing about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which case of the משנה the מחלוקת is about. It rules out the first case, where he claims and she denies, because no גט is needed there at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: On which case? If you say on the first part of the משנה, there is no 'we force' and no 'we request' there!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where this מחלוקת belongs, and right away rules out the first case of the משנה. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first case, he says 'I betrothed you' and she says 'you did not.' Going by her own words, she is not married, so she may marry anyone. She does not need a גט at all, so there is nothing to force or ask for.

keyTerms.meaning: On which one? To which case does this refer?
If you say. Brings up a possibility in order to test it
The first part of the משנה

phrases.english: On which case?
If you say on the first part,
phrases.notes: The first part: he says 'I betrothed you,' and she says 'you did not betroth me.'

phrases.english: there is no "we force"
and there is no "we request"!
phrases.notes: By her own words she is not married, so she does not need a גט from him at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what the מחלוקת of step 18 refers to.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which case of the משנה are רב and שמואל arguing about?

steps.title: They argue about the second case
steps.stepSummary: The מחלוקת is about the later case, where she says he betrothed her and he denies it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is about the later part of the משנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב and שמואל are talking about the case where she claims to be married and he denies it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In that case her own words bind her. She treats herself as a married woman, so she cannot marry anyone else without a גט. That is why it makes sense to ask whether the בית דין forces him or only asks him to free her.

keyTerms.meaning: The later part of the משנה

phrases.english: Rather, on the later part.
phrases.notes: The later part: she says 'you betrothed me,' and he says 'I did not.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The מחלוקת is about the case where she claims קידושין and he denies it.

steps.title: How can רב force him?
steps.stepSummary: Asking him to give a גט makes sense, but forcing him does not. He can say he does not want to become forbidden to her relatives.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, 'we request' is fine. But 'we force,' why? He can say: I do not want to become forbidden to her relatives.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב's view. It accepts שמואל's 'we ask,' but says forcing the man is unfair to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far he is allowed to marry her relatives, because he denies the קידושין. If he gives a גט, it looks like he admits he betrothed her. Then he becomes forbidden to her relatives, so he has a real reason to refuse, and we cannot force him.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted. This one works, but the other one is a problem
Fine, that works
I am not happy with it. I do not want it
Her relatives

phrases.english: Granted, "we request" is fine,
but "we force" — why?!
He can say: I am not happy
to become forbidden to her relatives.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that we know the case, challenges רב's ruling within it.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that the בית דין forces the man to give a גט in the case where she claims קידושין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A גט would act as an admission of קידושין and make her relatives forbidden to him. He has a fair reason to refuse, so he cannot be forced.

steps.title: Reworking the מחלוקת: גט and כתובה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the two rulings were really said one after the other. שמואל: we ask him to give a גט. רב: if he gave a גט on his own, we force him to pay the כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the teachings were said one on top of the other. שמואל said: we ask him to give a גט. רב said: if he gave a גט on his own, we force him to give the כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the idea that רב and שמואל argue about the same thing. Their rulings were said one after the other: שמואל speaks about the גט, and רב adds a ruling about the כתובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees we only ask him for a גט, so the problem from step 21 is gone. רב's 'we force' now means something else. If the man chose on his own to give a גט, he has acted as if he admits the קידושין. So the בית דין makes him pay her כתובה as well.

keyTerms.meaning: The teachings were said one on top of the other, not as an argument
Bill of divorce
On his own, without being asked
The marriage contract payment owed to a wife

steps.whatToRemember: In the end there is no clash. We only ask the man for a גט. But if he gives one on his own, he acts as if he admits the קידושין, and then he must also pay her כתובה.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that what a person does, like giving a גט, can count as an admission even if he never says 'I betrothed her.'

phrases.english: Rather: the teachings were said one on top of the other,
phrases.notes: He means the two rulings were said one after the other about different things, not as two sides of one argument.

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
We request of him to give a get.
Rav said:
If he gave a get on his own,
we force him to give the ketubah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 21 by reworking how the rulings of step 18 were said.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the statements: two separate rulings said one after the other, not opposing views on one question.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב and שמואל argued over whether the בית דין forces or only asks the man to give a גט.
steps.terutzMaskana: Everyone agrees we only ask him for a גט. רב adds that if he gives a גט on his own, it counts as an admission, and he is forced to pay the כתובה.

steps.title: Another report of רב: 'We force and we ask'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings another report of רב's words, saying בית דין both forces and asks. This backs up the idea from step 22 that two separate rulings were said.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also reported: רב אחא בר אדא said in the name of רב (and some say: רב אחא בר אדא said in the name of רב המנונא, in the name of רב): We force, and we ask.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second report of רב's teaching that mentions both forcing and asking. It supports the two-part explanation from step 22.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 22 the גמרא said 'asking' was about the גט and 'forcing' was about the כתובה. This report has רב himself mentioning both words, which fits that explanation. The chain of names is given in two versions.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also stated. This brings another report that fits what was just said.
We force (בית דין compels him)
We ask, meaning a request only, with no force

phrases.english: It was also stated:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר אַדָּא אָמַר רַב,
phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Adda said that Rav said,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר אַדָּא
phrases.english: and some say: Rav Acha bar Adda said
that Rav Hamnuna said that Rav said:
We force and we ask.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a second report of רב that supports the two-part reading given in step 22.
steps.raayaObject: The explanation that 'asking' and 'forcing' are two separate rulings about two different things.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A second report of רב's statement, through רב אחא בר אדא, saying 'כופין ומבקשין'.

steps.title: How can he both force and ask?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא is puzzled: forcing and asking contradict each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two things?! (How can he both force and ask?)
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that 'we force' and 'we ask' do not fit together as one ruling. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If בית דין forces him, there is no reason to ask. If it only asks, then it is not forcing. So the two words cannot describe one action.

keyTerms.meaning: Two (things)? This asks how two opposite rulings can both be true.

phrases.english: Two things?!
phrases.notes: He means: forcing and asking are opposites, so which is it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of the report just brought.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Forcing and asking cannot both apply to the same act.

steps.title: Ask for the גט, force payment of the כתובה
steps.stepSummary: The two words refer to two different things. בית דין asks him for a גט, and if he gives one on his own, it forces him to pay the כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he means: We ask him to give a גט, and if he gave one on his own, we force him to give the כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that 'asking' is about the גט and 'forcing' is about the כתובה money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The contradiction goes away because each word goes with a different thing. This is the same split described in step 22, so רב and שמואל do not really disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he means. It explains a statement that was unclear.
On his own, without being forced
The marriage contract money owed to the woman

steps.whatToRemember: In the case where she says there was קידושין and he denies it, בית דין asks him to give a גט. If he gives it on his own, he is forced to pay the כתובה.

phrases.english: This is what he is saying:
We ask of him to give a bill of divorce,
and if he gave it on his own,
we force him to give the marriage contract payment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'two things' challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the two words between two different things (the גט and the כתובה)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Forcing and asking both described one action, which made no sense.
steps.terutzMaskana: Asking is about the גט. Forcing is about the כתובה once he has given a גט on his own.

steps.title: קידושין with one witness does not count
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה rules that קידושין done in front of only one witness is not taken seriously at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: Someone who does קידושין in front of one witness, we are not concerned about his קידושין.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רב יהודה rules that קידושין in front of one witness has no effect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קידושין needs two witnesses to take effect. With only one, we do not even worry that it might have worked.

keyTerms.meaning: One who betroths (does קידושין)
One witness
We are not concerned. It is treated as having no effect.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
One who betroths with one witness,
we are not concerned about his betrothal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קידושין in front of only one witness is not taken seriously.

steps.title: What if both of them admit it?
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה is asked what the law is when both the man and the woman agree that קידושין happened.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked רב יהודה: If both of them admit it, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה is asked whether his rule still holds when both sides agree there was קידושין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Maybe one witness is not enough only when one side denies it. But if both agree, perhaps their agreement makes it count.

keyTerms.meaning: They asked him
Both of them admit it

phrases.english: They asked Rav Yehuda:
If both of them admit it, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how far רב יהודה's rule goes.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does one-witness קידושין count when both sides admit it took place?

steps.title: רב יהודה is unsure
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה answered 'yes and no'. He was unsure.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said 'yes' and 'no', and the matter was unclear to him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה cannot give a clear answer. The next step settles the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His 'yes and no' shows he saw reasons for both sides. That leaves room for the next step to settle the question.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes and no
It was weak in his hand. He was not sure.

phrases.english: Yes and no,
and it was unclear to him.
phrases.notes: Literally 'it was loose in his hand.' He could not decide.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the question, but without settling it.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No clear answer. רב יהודה was unsure.

steps.title: שמואל: not even if both admit
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן reports in the name of שמואל that one-witness קידושין does not count, even when both sides admit it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: רב נחמן said in the name of שמואל: Someone who does קידושין in front of one witness, we are not concerned about his קידושין, even if both of them admit it.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל settles the question רב יהודה left open. Even if both sides agree, one-witness קידושין does not count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'even if both admit' answer exactly what was asked in step 27. Without two witnesses there is no קידושין, whatever the two people say.

keyTerms.meaning: And even

phrases.aramaic: אִיתְּמַר, אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: It was stated: Rav Nachman said that Shmuel said:
One who betroths with one witness,
we are not concerned about his betrothal,
and even if both of them admit it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר, אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the question that רב יהודה left open.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One-witness קידושין has no effect even when both sides admit it.

steps.title: רבא challenges from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבא argues that the משנה's case, where he says 'I betrothed you' and she denies it, must have had one witness. Yet he is still bound by it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא challenged רב נחמן from the משנה: If he says 'I betrothed you' and she says 'you did not', he is forbidden to her relatives and she is permitted to his relatives. If there were witnesses, why is she permitted to his relatives? If there were no witnesses, why is he forbidden to hers? It must be a case of one witness!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא uses the משנה to argue that one-witness קידושין does have some effect, at least on the man who admits it. That goes against שמואל's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With two witnesses, the קידושין would be fully real, and she would be forbidden too. With no witnesses at all, there would be nothing to bind him. So רבא says the middle result must come from one witness, which shows one-witness קידושין is taken seriously against the man who admits it.

keyTerms.meaning: Her relatives (such as her sister or mother)
Why?
Rather, is it not...? This pushes for the only option left.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the man is forbidden to her relatives because the קידושין truly worked. He is bound only by his own claim. That is why she, who denies it, stays permitted.

phrases.english: Rava challenged Rav Nachman:
One who says to a woman, 'I betrothed you,'
and she says, 'You did not betroth me,'
he is forbidden to her relatives
and she is permitted to his relatives.
If there are witnesses,
why is she permitted to his relatives?
And if there are no witnesses,
why is he forbidden to her relatives?
Rather, is it not with one witness!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks שמואל's ruling, as reported by רב נחמן, using the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that one-witness קידושין has no effect at all
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's half-effect only makes sense with one witness. That would show one-witness קידושין does matter, at least for the man who admits it.

steps.title: Two witnesses who went overseas
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה is about a man who says there were two witnesses, but they went overseas and cannot be asked.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are we dealing with here? A case where he told her 'I betrothed you in front of so-and-so and so-and-so', and they went away overseas.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows there is a third possibility. There were two witnesses, but they are not available, so the משנה is not about one witness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He claims the קידושין was done properly, with two witnesses, so his own words bind him. Since the witnesses are gone, nothing is proven against her, and she stays permitted. The משנה says nothing about one-witness קידושין, so שמואל's ruling stands.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? This narrows the case to answer a question.
So-and-so and so-and-so (two named people)
Overseas, a faraway place

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל's rule stands: קידושין with one witness does not count, even if both admit it. The משנה's case is two witnesses who are unavailable.

phrases.english: What are we dealing with here?
Such as where he said to her,
'I betrothed you in front of so-and-so and so-and-so,'
and they went away overseas.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's challenge by redefining the case in the משנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה must be about one witness, so one-witness קידושין matters.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about two witnesses who are unavailable. He is bound by his own claim of valid קידושין, and the משנה proves nothing about one witness.

steps.title: Challenge from the divorced couple at the inn
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes a משנה where בית שמאי and בית הלל argue about whether a divorced woman who lodged with her ex-husband needs a second גט. He argues the case must involve one witness, which would show that one witness can make קידושין count.
steps.simpleTranslation: He challenged him: If a man divorces his wife and she then spends the night with him at an inn, בית שמאי say she does not need a second גט from him, and בית הלל say she does need a second גט. What is the case? If there are witnesses, what is בית שמאי's reason? If there are no witnesses, what is בית הלל's reason? So it must be talking about one witness!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a משנה to attack רב נחמן's rule that one-witness קידושין does not count. He argues that this משנה only makes sense if exactly one witness was there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With two witnesses, everyone would agree she was remarried, so בית שמאי's lenient view makes no sense. With no witnesses, there is nothing to worry about, so בית הלל's strict view makes no sense. The only middle case is one witness, and בית הלל take it seriously, which would mean one witness can create קידושין.

keyTerms.meaning: An inn
A second bill of divorce
What are the circumstances? What exactly is the case?
A single witness

phrases.english: He raised an objection to him:
phrases.notes: רבא is now challenging רב נחמן's teaching in the name of שמואל from Step 29.

phrases.english: One who divorces his wife
and she spent the night with him at an inn,
Beit Shammai say:
She does not need a second bill of divorce from him,
and Beit Hillel say:
She needs a second bill of divorce from him.
What are the circumstances?
If there are witnesses,
phrases.notes: He means witnesses who saw them be together as a way of doing קידושין.

phrases.english: what is the reason of Beit Shammai?
And if there are no witnesses,
what is the reason of Beit Hillel?
Rather, is it not about a case of one witness!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first challenge (Steps 30-31) was answered, a new challenge is brought against רב נחמן's rule from a different משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן in the name of שמואל: one-witness קידושין does not count.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's dispute only works with one witness, and בית הלל still require a second גט, which shows one witness can make קידושין count.

steps.title: The end of the same משנה shows it is not about one witness
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers from the end of the same משנה: בית הלל agree that a woman divorced after only אירוסין does not need a second גט. If one witness were the issue, that difference would make no sense.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to your reasoning, look at the end of the משנה: They agree that a woman divorced from אירוסין does not need a second גט from him, because he is not familiar with her. If you think one witness is believed, what difference is there between אירוסין and נשואין?
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן pushes back on רבא's proof by quoting the end of the same משנה. He shows that the one-witness reading does not fit it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The end of the משנה makes the law depend on whether he is used to her: after full marriage he is, after only אירוסין he is not. If the case were about a single witness who saw relations, it would not matter how familiar they were. So the משנה must be about guessing what happened, not about one witness to relations, and רבא's proof falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your own reasoning
The end part of a משנה or ברייתא
Betrothal, the first stage of marriage
Full marriage, after living together
He is not familiar or comfortable with her

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning,
say the end of that teaching:
And they agree about a woman who was divorced after betrothal
phrases.notes: "They agree" means בית הלל agree with בית שמאי in this case.

phrases.english: that she does not need a second bill of divorce from him,
because he is not familiar with her.
And if it enters your mind
that one witness is believed,
what difference is it to me if it is after betrothal,
what difference is it to me if it is after marriage?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's challenge by showing the end of the same משנה does not fit a one-witness case.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the inn משנה is about one witness.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A one-witness reading cannot explain why the law changes between a woman divorced after אירוסין and one divorced after נשואין.

steps.title: The case: witnesses to seclusion, but none to relations
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the משנה: there were witnesses that the couple was alone together (יחוד), but no witnesses to relations (ביאה). בית שמאי and בית הלל argue about what we may assume from that.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what case are we dealing with here? Where there are witnesses that they were alone together, but there are no witnesses that they had relations. בית שמאי hold: one does not...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new explanation of the משנה that has nothing to do with one witness. It then starts explaining בית שמאי's view, which continues past this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the case is about two proper witnesses who saw them go off alone, without seeing anything more. The argument is whether being alone together is enough to assume they had relations for קידושין. This removes רבא's challenge, so רב נחמן's rule stands.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here?
Witnesses who saw a man and woman go off alone together
Witnesses to the act of relations itself
They hold, their opinion is

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the witnesses here are one witness. There are full witnesses, but they only saw the couple alone together, not anything more. The argument is about what we assume from that.
steps.whyThisMatters: This reading means the משנה is not a proof that one witness makes קידושין count, so רב נחמן's teaching from שמואל survives the challenge.

phrases.english: Rather, what case are we dealing with here?
Where there are witnesses to their being alone together
but there are no witnesses to relations.
Beit Shammai hold: one does not

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting the one-witness reading, the גמרא gives the correct case behind the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case of the משנה (אוקימתא).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא thought the משנה must be about one witness, which would show that one witness can make קידושין count.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about witnesses to seclusion without witnesses to relations, so it says nothing about one witness.
